rules.name: Catastrophic hazard over facility
rules.metric: highest hazard level at facility (1-5)
rules.basis: NWS classification: Hurricane/Storm Surge/Extreme Wind Warning, or flash-flood/tornado emergency wording. Operating while one covers the facility is treated as life-threatening. Level mapping is a PROTOTYPE ASSUMPTION (not official USDA/OPM policy)
rules.why_this_threshold: Employees should not be asked to commute into, or occupy, a facility under a catastrophic-class warning.

rules.name: Sustained warning-level hazard over facility
rules.metric: hours the warning persists into the operating window
rules.comparator: <= delays / > telework; arrives mid-day -> early dismissal
rules.basis: NWS Warning-class product (flash flood, winter storm/ice/blizzard, tropical storm warning) covering the facility. The 4h persistence cut-off is a PROTOTYPE ASSUMPTION (not official USDA/OPM policy)
rules.why_this_threshold: A hazard that clears within a few hours justifies a delay; one that persists makes commuting unreasonable; one arriving mid-day calls for an early release.

rules.name: Short-fuse warning over facility
rules.metric: tornado / severe thunderstorm warnings covering facility
rules.basis: NWS Tornado / Severe Thunderstorm Warning. Short-fuse warnings (minutes-1h) trigger shelter-in-place, not a status change. PROTOTYPE ASSUMPTION (not official USDA/OPM policy)
rules.why_this_threshold: Closing for a warning that expires in under an hour is disproportionate; protecting people in the building right now is not.

rules.name: Workforce commute exposure -> closure
rules.metric: % workforce with HIGH commute risk (home/route inside a Warning-level travel hazard)
rules.basis: Sector 'service_center' parameter; only when the hazard persists beyond 4h of opening or its end is unknown. PROTOTYPE ASSUMPTION (not official USDA/OPM policy)
rules.why_this_threshold: Customers arrive unannounced and cannot be pre-warned, so the office acts earlier on facility-area hazards and has no round-the-clock essential minimum.

rules.name: Workforce commute exposure -> unscheduled leave/telework
rules.metric: % workforce with HIGH or ELEVATED commute risk
rules.basis: Sector 'service_center' parameter; applies when the hazard persists beyond 4h of opening or its end is unknown (clears_in=Noneh). PROTOTYPE ASSUMPTION (not official USDA/OPM policy)
rules.why_this_threshold: When a sizeable share of staff face a hazardous commute, voluntary leave/telework removes them from harm without a formal closure.

rules.name: Workforce commute exposure -> delayed arrival
rules.metric: % workforce with HIGH or ELEVATED commute risk
rules.basis: Sector 'service_center' parameter; hazard must clear within 4h of opening (clears_in=Noneh) and the facility must not already be open. PROTOTYPE ASSUMPTION (not official USDA/OPM policy)
rules.why_this_threshold: A short-lived commute hazard (e.g. morning ice or fog) is best handled by delaying arrival until it clears.

rules.name: Verified road closures near facility
rules.metric: full road closures within radius
rules.comparator: n/a
rules.basis: NOT EVALUATED: No archived 511 road data is available for this historical scenario.
rules.why_this_threshold: Commute safety is inferred from weather-alert geometry only.

alternatives_considered.why: R6: tornado / severe thunderstorm warnings covering facility = 0 (needs >= 1); R5: % workforce with HIGH or ELEVATED commute risk = 0.0 (needs >= 10)
R4: % workforce with HIGH or ELEVATED commute risk = 0.0 (needs >= 15)
no rule supports this level
R1: highest hazard level at facility (1-5) = 0 (needs >= 5); R3: % workforce with HIGH commute risk (home/route inside a Warning-level travel hazard) = 0.0 (needs >= 40)

sector_playbook.normal: Open; keep lobby staff aware of active watches.
sector_playbook.delayed_arrival: Open late; post notice on door/phone line; reschedule appointments.
sector_playbook.telework: Move to phones/online services; close lobby to walk-ins; forward office line.
sector_playbook.early_dismissal: Close lobby first, release staff in waves; confirm no customers remain.
sector_playbook.closure: Close to the public; staff stay home; post status on the service-center line and website.

rules.basis: NWS classification: Hurricane/Storm Surge/Extreme Wind Warning, or flash-flood/tornado emergency wording. Operating while one covers the facility is treated as life-threatening. Level mapping is a PROTOTYPE ASSUMPTION (not official USDA/OPM policy)
rules.why_this_threshold: Employees should not be asked to commute into, or occupy, a facility under a catastrophic-class warning.

rules.name: Sustained warning-level hazard over facility
rules.metric: hours the warning persists into the operating window
rules.comparator: <= delays / > telework; arrives mid-day -> early dismissal
rules.basis: NWS Warning-class product (flash flood, winter storm/ice/blizzard, tropical storm warning) covering the facility. The 4h persistence cut-off is a PROTOTYPE ASSUMPTION (not official USDA/OPM policy)
rules.why_this_threshold: A hazard that clears within a few hours justifies a delay; one that persists makes commuting unreasonable; one arriving mid-day calls for an early release.

rules.name: Short-fuse warning over facility
rules.metric: tornado / severe thunderstorm warnings covering facility
rules.basis: NWS Tornado / Severe Thunderstorm Warning. Short-fuse warnings (minutes-1h) trigger shelter-in-place, not a status change. PROTOTYPE ASSUMPTION (not official USDA/OPM policy)
rules.why_this_threshold: Closing for a warning that expires in under an hour is disproportionate; protecting people in the building right now is not.

rules.name: Workforce commute exposure -> closure
rules.metric: % workforce with HIGH commute risk (home/route inside a Warning-level travel hazard)
rules.basis: Sector 'service_center' parameter; only when the hazard persists beyond 4h of opening or its end is unknown. PROTOTYPE ASSUMPTION (not official USDA/OPM policy)
rules.why_this_threshold: Customers arrive unannounced and cannot be pre-warned, so the office acts earlier on facility-area hazards and has no round-the-clock essential minimum.

rules.name: Workforce commute exposure -> unscheduled leave/telework
rules.metric: % workforce with HIGH or ELEVATED commute risk
rules.basis: Sector 'service_center' parameter; applies when the hazard persists beyond 4h of opening or its end is unknown (clears_in=Noneh). PROTOTYPE ASSUMPTION (not official USDA/OPM policy)
rules.why_this_threshold: When a sizeable share of staff face a hazardous commute, voluntary leave/telework removes them from harm without a formal closure.

rules.name: Workforce commute exposure -> delayed arrival
rules.metric: % workforce with HIGH or ELEVATED commute risk
rules.basis: Sector 'service_center' parameter; hazard must clear within 4h of opening (clears_in=Noneh) and the facility must not already be open. PROTOTYPE ASSUMPTION (not official USDA/OPM policy)
rules.why_this_threshold: A short-lived commute hazard (e.g. morning ice or fog) is best handled by delaying arrival until it clears.

rules.name: Verified road closures near facility
rules.metric: full road closures within radius
rules.comparator: n/a
rules.basis: NOT EVALUATED: No archived 511 road data is available for this historical scenario.
